note: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl, cached at runs/theory-tests/r4m01/base01_F_math500.jsonl. When I opened it to check the format, the stored file had 500 rows, all with sample == 0, so there is one row per problem. In that case no problem has both a cap_hit true row and a cap_hit false row, and the within-problem pair the recipe needs does not exist. The script implements the recipe in full: group by problem_index, C = cap-hit row with the lowest sample, F = finished row with len(text) >= 3000 and the lowest sample, ratio = zlib level 9 bytes over UTF-8 bytes of text[:3000], ties count 0.5. If no problem qualifies it prints not_computable and does not use another file. The inventory says 1 to 4 samples per problem may have been planned, but only sample 0 is stored. No alternative reading was computed (alt_measured null).

File: Modal iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl (500 rows, base cue, T 0.6 / top-p 1.0), cached at runs/theory-tests/r4m01/d4fa/answers.jsonl. Rows kept: len(text) >= 6000 and either loop_A false, or loop_A true with onset_A_char not null and >= 7000. Rows with loop_A missing are dropped, but none were seen. s = zlib-9 ratio of text[:6000] in UTF-8 bytes. AUROC of -s for loop_A true is computed by full pairwise Mann-Whitney with ties counting 0.5. The stored text starts with the cue's prefill tail (' line!'), and onset_A_char is taken to be measured in the same text. The text is used as stored. The recipe seemed clear to me, so alt_measured is null. The counts of kept rows and positives are printed and included in the JSON.

Files: s3 .../r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (base, cue) and s3 .../r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (RL step 2800, plain), cached under runs/theory-tests/r4m01/. Each file holds 500 rows, all sample 0. Rows are paired by problem_index, and a pair is kept only when both texts are >= 3000 characters. The score is 1 if ratio(base[:3000]) < ratio(rl[:3000]), 0.5 if equal, else 0. If a file has duplicate sample-0 rows the first is kept and a warning is printed. The base text starts with the cue's prefill tail (' line!'), which adds a few characters that differ from RL's text. It is used as stored, as the recipe says. The kept pairs are only problems where both models wrote at least 3000 characters, so they lean toward hard problems. alt_measured is null.

Files: s3 .../r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_own.jsonl and K_rl.jsonl (78 rows each), cached under runs/theory-tests/r4m01/. The stored text includes the given prefix (n_answer_tokens = n_prefix + n_new). With n_prefix in the thousands of tokens, text[:3000] is almost entirely the prefix: for K_own it is the base's own earlier text, and for K_rl it is RL's text. The text is used as stored, as the recipe says. Filter: len(text) >= 3000, and drop rows with loop_A true and onset_A_char null or < 4000. Per-file AUROC of -s for cap_hit uses Mann-Whitney with ties counting 0.5. measured is the unweighted mean of the defined per-file AUROCs, or the single defined one. If both are undefined the script prints not_computable. Each file's AUROC and counts are printed. The loop filter drops looped rows, and those are mostly cap hits, so the cap-hit group that remains comes from late loops and loop-free cap hits. alt_measured is a different reading: one AUROC over the kept rows of both files pooled.
